headline: The nightly bot takes out its own trash — a squatted port can't wedge the nightly anymore
lede: Last week the nightly bot correctly refused to play against a server it did not spawn (#1312's law) — but when the squatter was provably the factory's own abandoned wreckage, night after night still went dark waiting for a human. Now the bot proves the difference between its own orphaned debris and a stranger, reclaims the port, and lets the alarm expire on its own. Meanwhile Britannia got its passage made seen: moored boat, wind-set sail, coin arc, and a captain with a deny voice of his own.

notes.text: #2344 fixed + hardened: the :5199 squatter (an orphaned npm dev server with a dead process-group leader) was killed, and nightlybot gained classifyOrphan — reclaim only when it is OUR port, OUR launch signature, and the launcher is provably gone. A stranger hosted by a live session still aborts the run; the stage-2 ownership proof still gates every game played. Live-tested both directions: synthetic orphan reclaimed, live squat refused.
Squat alarms now expire with their proof: any completed non-mutated nightly closes open squatter issues, so the board can't read a healed port as haunted. nightlybotcheck 40→50.
#1711 unchanged Jon-side: clap-test on the phone (#2156) + SESSION_WRITE_KEY deploy, then the relabel one-off; jonq #2305 open to the 17th.
